goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:12) uses `cook_method :raw_html` with no sanitization for the RSS feed path, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `raw post.cooked`, yielding stored XSS from a poisoned feed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `PostCreator` is invoked with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` short-circuits to `return raw` for `:raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The RSS polling job (`Jobs::PollFeed`) feeds `TopicEmbed.import` with `i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM URL. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output that untrusted HTML directly. This is a classic stored XSS path if the feed content is poisoned (e.g., `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes), and no sanitization is performed anywhere in this diff for the `raw_html` cook method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-38` calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` unconditionally even when `revisor.revise!` returns false without saving, permanently marking stale content as applied

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s `content_sha1` differs, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether `revise!` succeeded. `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (it explicitly does `return false if not should_revise?`), meaning no save/update occurred, yet `content_sha1` will still be updated in the database. That can cause the embed to be marked as up-to-date even though the post content was not actually revised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29` uses non-atomic `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `expire`; a crash between them leaves the key without a TTL, throttling that embed_url forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward is a TTL applied via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands, so if the process crashes or errors between them, the key can remain without an expiration. Because subsequent calls will see the key exists and return `true` (throttled), that embed_url could be throttled indefinitely until the key is manually deleted or Redis is flushed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:16-31` does check-then-insert on `embed_url` without handling the unique index, so concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs create duplicate topics and raise `RecordNotUnique`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank it enters a transaction and later does `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). With concurrent callers (e.g., multiple `RetrieveTopic` jobs for the same `embed_url`), both can observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; one will win and the other will raise an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or similar) because the code does not rescue/retry around the unique constraint. The “duplicate topics” part is less certain because the surrounding transaction may roll back the topic/post creation on exception, but the unhandled unique-violation race is a real, verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20` compares `URI(request.referer || '').host` exactly against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, rejecting subdomain/`www.` variants and hard-failing with InvalidAccess when the Referer header is stripped

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `ensure_embeddable` that raises `InvalidAccess` unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so it will indeed reject `www.`/subdomain variants and will fail when `Referer` is missing (nil host). However, this behavior is an intentional security gate for embedding: without a referer/host match, the server cannot verify the embedding origin, and `embeddable_host` is explicitly a single host setting (admin can configure the exact host they want to allow). The finding characterizes these deliberate constraints as a defect without evidence they are unintended or incorrect per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Gemfile:209-211` adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` but not `Gemfile.lock`, breaking `bundle install --deployment`/frozen checks for the default Rails 3 bundle

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new gems to `Gemfile` but only updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. There is no corresponding update to the default lockfile (`Gemfile.lock`) in this diff, so in any setup that uses the standard Bundler workflow (Gemfile + Gemfile.lock, especially with `--deployment`/frozen settings), the lockfile would be out of sync with the Gemfile and bundler would fail or refuse to install. The diff itself shows the mismatch (Gemfile changed, only rails4 lock updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,143` drops the `--category` option and `created_at: Date.parse(...)` when switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, so imported topics lose original timestamps and category placement

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `--category` option is removed and the previous logic that resolved `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)` is deleted. The call that created the topic with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is also removed. It is replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and in TopicEmbed.import_remote/import the PostCreator is invoked without `created_at` or `category`. Therefore Disqus imports will no longer preserve original thread timestamps and cannot place topics into the requested category (they’ll use defaults/current time).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9` reloads every 30s unconditionally with no attempt cap, so permanently failing retrieval makes every visitor's iframe poll the forum forever

adjudication.rationale: In the new view `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the script does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` inside an IIFE and there is no counter/attempt limit or stop condition. This template is rendered by `EmbedController#best` when no `topic_id` is found (and a background retrieval job is enqueued). If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., invalid URL, fetch failure, misconfiguration), the iframe will keep reloading every 30 seconds indefinitely for each visitor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:12` mutates the caller's string via `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, modifying PollFeed/import_remote buffers and raising on frozen string literals; should use `contents + ...`

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << ...` does mutate the passed-in String, which is a verifiable behavior. However, in the diff the callers (`Jobs::PollFeed` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) pass freshly created strings (`CGI.unescapeHTML(...)` and `doc.content`) and do not reuse them afterward, so the mutation does not introduce a clear correctness/security defect in the shown code. The claim about “raising on frozen string literals” is speculative: there is no `# frozen_string_literal: true` pragma in this file/diff, nor any evidence callers pass frozen strings here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `absolutize_urls` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:56` only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with `/`, leaving document-relative URLs like `images/foo.png` or `../x` broken

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code only rewrites `href`/`src` values when they `start_with?('/')`. That covers root-relative URLs (e.g., `/images/x.png`) but does not handle other valid relative forms like `images/foo.png`, `./x`, or `../x`. Since the method comment explicitly says “Convert any relative URLs to absolute” and this method is used when importing feed/article HTML, leaving these other relative URLs untouched can result in broken links/images in the imported content. This is directly verifiable from the conditions in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5` has no null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`, so `comments.appendChild` throws and breaks the host page's JS if the container is missing

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the embedding page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and calling `appendChild` will throw a runtime error, potentially breaking JS execution on the host page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46` asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`/`retrieve` while the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, passing only incidentally and never covering the job-argument contract; there is no spec for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct: `EmbedController#best` does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` at all when `topic_id` is nil; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and renders `loading`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work...” example) expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. That expectation will never be met given the controller code in this diff, so the spec is incorrect/out-of-sync and would fail. It’s also true that the new `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job has no dedicated spec to verify the argument/behavior contract, though the primary verifiable defect here is the mismatched controller spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` lacks coverage for the refused-`revise!` update path, non-default ports in `absolutize_urls`, and duplicate-URL imports

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` with some coverage (malformed URL, new import, updating when content changes, and URL absolutization for default ports). It does not include explicit tests for: (1) a `PostRevisor#revise!` failure/early-return path, (2) `absolutize_urls` with non-default ports, or (3) importing the same URL again without changes (duplicate/no-op). However, these are test-coverage gaps rather than a clear defect/bug/security issue proven by the diff itself; the code can still be correct without those additional specs. The finding is therefore not a “real problem” in the sense of identifying an introduced defect.
